kind: lookup: single document, two-part fact on one page, with a same-group distractor paper in the corpus
question: How many human design sequences are in the Fusion 360 Gallery reconstruction dataset, and which two modeling operations does its domain-specific language support?
grading_notes: Both parts are required. The dataset holds 8,625 human design sequences, and its language supports just the sketch and extrude modeling operations (Fusion 360 Gallery paper, page 1). The corpus also holds the JoinABLe paper, which describes a different dataset from the same project, the Fusion 360 Gallery ASSEMBLY dataset; a count taken from that paper is wrong. kind: lookup: numeric result in the body of a paper, present in two copies of the paper, with nearby distractor numbers
question: In the VIPER work on extracting decision-tree policies, how big was the decision tree learned for Atari Pong and what reward did it reach?
grading_notes: The decision tree for Atari Pong (symbolic state space) has 769 nodes and achieves a perfect reward of 21.0, averaged over 50 rollouts, the same as the deep Q-network oracle (page 7 of either copy of the VIPER paper). Both the size and the reward are required. Nearby distractors that FAIL if given as the Atari Pong answer: the 31-node tree for the toy Pong model (reward 250), the cart-pole trees (reward 200), and the 7967-node DAGGER tree that page 9 compares against. A refusal fails.
required_points: the Atari Pong decision tree has 769 nodes
it achieves a perfect reward of 21.0 (matching the DQN oracle)

kind: synthesis: two papers on the same problem, neither named in the question; symbolic versus neural approach
question: Two papers in this collection automatically correct incorrect student programs from introductory programming courses, one with symbolic program synthesis and one with a neural network. What does each approach need from the instructor, and what fraction of incorrect submissions did each correct?
grading_notes: Symbolic approach (Singh, Gulwani and Solar-Lezama, automated feedback generation): the instructor must supply a reference implementation of the assignment and an error model, written as correction rules, describing the mistakes students might make; it corrected on average 65% of incorrect submissions. Neural approach (sk_p, Pu et al.): needs no manual, problem-specific correction strategies; a seq2seq model is trained on earlier student submissions and candidate fixes are checked against a test suite; it corrected 29% of incorrect submissions. All four facts are required, and each figure must be attached to the right approach. The sk_p introduction itself describes the earlier approach's error-model requirement, so that fact may be cited from either paper, but the 65% figure exists only in the Singh paper. An answer covering only one of the two papers fails.
required_points: the symbolic approach needs a reference implementation and an error model of correction rules from the instructor
the symbolic approach corrected on average 65% of incorrect submissions
the neural approach (sk_p) needs no manual, problem-specific correction strategies, only prior submissions and a test suite
the neural approach corrected 29% of incorrect submissions

kind: synthesis: aggregation across four papers, more sources than the six-chunk budget can hold
question: Which papers in this collection use program synthesis or programmatic representations to make reinforcement learning policies safer or better at generalizing, and what form does the synthesized program or policy take in each?
grading_notes: The corpus holds four such papers. (1) VIPER (Bastani, Pu, Solar-Lezama): decision-tree policies distilled from a DNN oracle so they can be verified. (2) Synthesizing Programmatic Policies that Inductively Generalize (Inala et al., ICLR 2020): programmatic state machine policies, learned by adaptive teaching, that generalize to any number of repetitions. (3) Program Synthesis Guided Reinforcement Learning for Partially Observed Environments (Yang et al.): model predictive program synthesis, which synthesizes the guiding program, a sequence of DSL components, instead of having the user write it. (4) Neurosymbolic Transformers for Multi-Agent Communication (Inala, Yang et al.): a programmatic communication policy that hardens a transformer's soft communication graph. PASS requires at least three of the four, each with the correct form of program or policy. Also acceptable, as extras, are the two shielding papers (verifiably safe exploration; safe human-interactive control) if described accurately as enforcing constraints rather than synthesizing policies. FAIL if fewer than three are given, if a form is attributed to the wrong paper, or if a paper is invented.
required_points: VIPER: decision-tree policies extracted from a neural oracle, for verifiability
Inala et al. 2020: programmatic state machine policies for inductive generalization
Yang et al. 2021: the guiding program (a sequence of DSL components) is synthesized by model predictive program synthesis
Neurosymbolic Transformers: a programmatic communication policy combined with a transformer policy

kind: synthesis: how one idea changed between two papers four years apart, both by the same author
question: How did the correctness reference that a programmer supplies alongside a sketch change between the original 2005 StreamBit paper and the 2009 overview of the sketching approach?
grading_notes: In the 2005 paper (Programming by Sketching for Bit-Streaming Programs), the programmer writes clean, portable reference code, and the compiler fills in the sketch's missing details while ensuring the completed sketch is faithful to that input reference code. In the 2009 overview (The Sketching Approach to Program Synthesis), the programmer provides either a reference implementation or a set of test routines that the synthesized code must pass, and the Sketch synthesizer accepts specifications as parameterized or non-deterministic test harnesses. A correct answer states both positions and identifies the change: the 2009 system also accepts tests or test harnesses, not only a reference implementation. An answer describing only one paper fails.
required_points: 2005 StreamBit: the programmer supplies reference code and the compiler ensures the completed sketch is faithful to it
2009 Sketch: the programmer supplies either a reference implementation or a set of test routines/test harnesses the synthesized code must pass
identifies the change, that tests or test harnesses became an accepted alternative to a reference implementation

kind: conflicting versions: the corpus holds an arXiv and a conference version of one paper that give different figures
question: How many problems does LiveCodeBench contain, and what period do they cover?
grading_notes: The corpus holds two versions of the LiveCodeBench paper that disagree. The arXiv version (DBLP_journals_corr_abs-2403-07974.pdf) reports 511 problems from contests between May 2023 and May 2024. The ICLR 2025 version (DBLP_conf_iclr_JainHGLYZWSSS25.pdf) reports 612 problems from contests between May 2023 and August 2024; its appendix still carries a leftover sentence saying 511 problem instances. A correct answer either reports both figures and attributes each to its version, or reports one figure, names the version it came from, and notes that the benchmark is live and continuously updated. A single unqualified number fails, because the corpus does not support one. Blending the versions, such as 612 problems through May 2024, fails.
required_points: gives a problem count that matches one of the two versions (511 or 612)
gives the date range that belongs to that same version (May 2023 to May 2024 for 511; May 2023 to August 2024 for 612)
discloses that more than one version exists, or names the version the figure came from
